controls_available: Difficulty 1 uses four diamond targets, one screen stone, one lava hazard, one fragile-support block, durability margin 2, and unsealed targets.
Full interaction exposes horizontal canvas dragging for rotation and canvas clicking for frontmost-face mining.
The REBUILD MINE button resets the pile, camera, durability, inventory, and transcript.
The EXIT MINE button submits the transcript for administrative certification.
autonomous_processes: No outcome-affecting task process runs without a new agent action: orientation, voxels, durability, inventory, collapse state, and event history are changed only by direct handlers.

The compass has a short CSS transform transition after a rotation, and a failed submission can display a CSS failure animation; these are presentation effects and do not change the mine state or available actions.
The 180-second play allowance is a deadline, not a visibly evidenced non-clock task-state process.
grouped_control_modes: canvas_drag_rotation: a horizontal drag of at least 48 pixels changes the camera orientation by one quarter turn.
canvas_click_mining: a canvas click resolves the current frontmost visible voxel face and applies its mining result.
reset_button: rebuilds the generated pile and restores the starting state.
exit_button: posts the completed transcript for verification and is administrative rather than an outcome-phase action.

clause_i.reason: Any positive wait leaves the complete task model unchanged, so an observation-free q can choose no-op for every still-solvable history and defer the board-specific click or rotation to the continuation after observing the unchanged board. Therefore clause (i) does not rule out an observation-free policy.

clause_ii.reason: A current endpoint screenshot is sufficient to choose the same board-specific rotation or click after the wait because the pile and depth order remain unchanged; this is static visual sufficiency, not evidence of an autonomous process.

clause_iii.reason: There is no positive Delta during which a non-clock task-state process changes autonomously. The state mutations are synchronous in rotation, mining, and reset handlers, so Q for an available action and its advantage over no-op do not strictly decrease during an idle interval. The CSS transition, failure animation, and deadline do not satisfy this clause.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 activates four targets, one screen, one lava hazard, one support, durability margin 2, and sealed_targets false.
Both simplified and full interaction modes are implemented; the configured play allowance is 180 seconds with a zero-millisecond observation window and one frame.
The generator consumes only the supplied difficulty parameters, constructs a static voxel layout and click/rotation solution, and exports no timer, motion process, or autonomous update state.
Rotation, mining, and reset mutate the model synchronously inside direct event handlers; mining changes voxels, durability, inventory, or collapse only when a click occurs.
Full mode binds canvas drag to rotation and canvas click to mining, while reset and exit are explicit controls.
The only timed-looking effects are a compass presentation transition and a short failure animation; neither updates task state.
The grader replays the ordered rotate, reset, and mine events and checks ray hits, hazards, durability, inventory, and collapse without using elapsed time.
